title: I built a site where nobody can edit their trading track record. Tell me why it won't work.
author: Purple-Ad6867
selftext:
I got tired of signal sellers with screenshot track records. Winners posted, losers deleted.

So I built the opposite. You post a prediction before the open. It gets hash-locked — no backdating. The market settles it automatically. Everything stays: wins, losses, even the entries that never filled. No accounts. Free. Open source.

Almost called it StockOverflow. Went with QuantRank500 — felt more like a race than homework. Everyone gets the same simulated $500. My own bot is user #1.

Two questions for this crowd: what would it take for you to actually trust a record like this? And what's the first way someone will try to game it?

[demo.quantrank500.com](http://demo.quantrank500.com) if you want to poke it. Code's on GitHub.

comments.author: read_more_comments
comments.body: I can already do that on tradingview

replies.author: Purple-Ad6867
replies.body: You can, and TradingView is better at charting and paper trading — but here the call is sealed before the open and settled automatically, so it stays on the record either way. Same simulated $500 and same rules for everyone makes it a real competition, and nobody ranks until 33 calls have settled, so one lucky week isn't a track record. For people who just watch, that's the whole point: the complete history is public, losses included, so it's possible to tell who is actually worth following instead of guessing from screenshots.

comments.author: Exciting-World5861
comments.body: assuming it works correctly fetching the right data etc, what would be the incentive to use it, the sellers wouldn't want to display their record for the reasons you've said and regular traders would not want to publicly post their trades. it's essentially a lose-lose proposition you're offering

replies.author: Purple-Ad6867
replies.body:
You're right that established sellers won't join — they have an audience already and nothing to gain. They're not who this is for.

It's for two other groups: everyday investors, whose only options today are influencer screenshots and blind trust, and skilled forecasters — human or bot — who can call markets but have no audience and no credible way to prove it.

Predictions lock before the open, the market settles them, nothing is editable. Free and open, closer to Wikipedia than a product.

Early participants get the one thing that can't be bought later: a record with time behind it.
